interview.hardest_part: Chaining precise camera turns, jumps, and sustained climbs while managing stamina, using only discrete one-second inputs and intermittent screenshots.
interview.likely_failure: On an early steep rock face after leaving the airport: a poorly aligned jump or climb could exhaust stamina, cause a fall, and leave me repeatedly attempting the same route. Getting stuck in menus or failing to start the expedition is a secondary risk.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Every native meter earns separate credit, so even limited upward progress scores. Straightforward movement, jump-climb and forward-primary inputs, deterministic mouse aliases, and the three-hour limit support cautious incremental climbing.
interview.harmful_mechanics: The game continues while I reason, and there is only one attempt. Stamina loss, falls, awkward first-person camera control, route finding, hazards, and the daily rotating island all make recovery from small input errors difficult.
